Moved to the University of California at Berkeley.

people.name: Alexander Plunket Greene
people.bio: British businessman and partner of Mary Quant. He bought Markham House in 1955 for the Bazaar boutique.

milestones.event: Bought Markham House on the King's Road.

people.name: Robert Rauschenberg
people.bio: American artist. He joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958 and had his first solo show at Betty Parsons in 1951.

milestones.event: Joined the Leo Castelli Gallery.
Won the grand prize for painting at the Venice Biennale.

people.name: Robert Venturi
people.bio: American architect who argued for complexity and contradiction against the purity of Modernism.

photo.credit: todd sheridan from New York, United States

milestones.event: Completed the Vanna Venturi House in Philadelphia.
Published Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture.
Published Learning from Las Vegas with Denise Scott Brown and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Paul Bocuse
people.bio: French chef of Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or near Lyon. He made the Auberge du Pont de Collonges a three-star restaurant, cooked from the market and made the chef a public figure. He started the Bocuse d'Or in 1987.

milestones.event: The Auberge du Pont de Collonges won its third Michelin star.
Created the black truffle soup for a dinner at the Élysée Palace.

people.name: Verner Panton
people.bio: Danish furniture and lighting designer of bright, curved and one-piece plastic objects.

milestones.event: Drew the Panton chair, a cantilever seat in one shell.
Saw the Panton chair go into series production in moulded plastic.

people.name: Vivian Maier
people.bio: American street photographer whose work was found after her death.

milestones.event: Her negatives were bought at an auction in Chicago.

people.name: Thea Porter
people.bio: British designer, born in Jerusalem. Her long printed dresses and caftans of Middle Eastern cloth made her a maker of hippie and bohemian dress in London.

milestones.event: Sold caftans and long dresses of Middle Eastern cloth from her Soho shop in London.

people.name: Adrian Frutiger
people.bio: Swiss type designer whose Frutiger typeface, the humanist sans of airports and system interfaces, gave Frutiger Aero its name.

milestones.event: Released the Univers typeface.
Released the Frutiger typeface.

people.name: Agnès Varda
people.bio: Belgian-born French film director whose first film came before the New Wave.

milestones.event: Released La Pointe Courte.
Released Cléo from 5 to 7.

people.name: Alison Smithson
people.bio: English architect who, with Peter Smithson, started the New Brutalism.

milestones.event: Completed Hunstanton School with Peter Smithson.
Completed Robin Hood Gardens in London.

people.name: Andy Warhol
people.bio: American artist who used silkscreen and commercial images in Pop Art.

milestones.event: Showed Campbell's Soup Cans in Los Angeles.
Started to make silkscreen paintings and prints.
Opened the Factory studio in New York.

people.name: Christian Millau
people.bio: French food critic and writer. With Henri Gault he wrote the Gault Millau guide, which gave the new light kitchen of the 1970s a name and a list of rules.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Henri Gault.
Published with Gault the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Donald Judd
people.bio: American artist who turned a cast-iron factory building in SoHo into a home and studio and kept its open floors and large windows.

milestones.event: Bought 101 Spring Street, a five-storey cast-iron building in SoHo, New York.
Started to move his work and home to Marfa, Texas.

people.name: Garry Winogrand
people.bio: American street photographer of New York in the 1960s.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Documents exhibition at MoMA.

people.name: Nicolas Hayek
people.bio: Swiss businessman who took control of the Swiss watch industry group and put the Swatch at the centre of its recovery.

milestones.event: Took over the Swatch group.

people.name: Pierre Troisgros
people.bio: French chef of Roanne. With his brother Jean he ran the Frères Troisgros restaurant and made the salmon with sorrel sauce, a sauce that the cook did not thicken with flour. Some critics call him a father of nouvelle cuisine.

milestones.event: The Frères Troisgros restaurant in Roanne won its second Michelin star.
The restaurant won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Frank Gehry
people.bio: Canadian-American architect of sculptural forms clad in metal.

photo.credit: City of Toronto / Jose San Juan

milestones.event: Rebuilt his own house in Santa Monica with chain-link and corrugated metal.
Completed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao.

people.name: Grace Kelly
people.bio: American actress and Princess of Monaco. A photograph of her with a structured Hermès bag in 1956 made the bag known by her name.

milestones.event: Held a Hermès handbag in front of her body in a magazine photograph; the maker renamed the bag the Kelly.

people.name: Henri Gault
people.bio: French food critic. With Christian Millau he started the restaurant guide Le Nouveau Guide in 1969. He used the phrase nouvelle cuisine for the new light cooking of the chefs of his time.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Christian Millau.
Published with Millau the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Irving Blum
people.bio: American dealer of the Ferus Gallery. In 1962 he bought all 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings from Warhol.

milestones.event: Bought the 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings for 1,000 dollars.

people.name: Jasper Johns
people.bio: American artist. He joined the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1958.

milestones.event: Joined the Leo Castelli Gallery.

people.name: Jean-Luc Godard
people.bio: French-Swiss film director whose jump cuts broke the rules of film editing.

milestones.event: Released Breathless.
Released Pierrot le Fou.

people.name: Mary Quant
people.bio: British designer. Her boutique on the King's Road sold the miniskirt and the short shift to young London, and she made the street the source of the fashion.

milestones.event: Opened the boutique Bazaar on the King's Road, London.
Showed the Wet collection of PVC raincoats.
Received the OBE for services to fashion.

people.name: Robert Arneson
people.bio: American sculptor and teacher at the University of California, Davis. His glazed stoneware toilets, typewriters and self-portraits set the style of funk ceramics.

milestones.event: Began to teach ceramics at the University of California, Davis.
Made the glazed stoneware Typewriter.

people.name: Steve McQueen
people.bio: American film actor and racing driver. He wore a square Heuer chronograph in the racing film Le Mans, and the model took his name in the market.

milestones.event: Wore a square Heuer Monaco chronograph in the film Le Mans.

people.name: Bernd Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Hilla Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Hilla Becher.

people.name: Denise Scott Brown
people.bio: Zambian-born American architect and planner who studied the commercial strip as architecture.

milestones.event: Published Learning from Las Vegas with Robert Venturi and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Gérald Genta
people.bio: Swiss watch designer. He drew the Royal Oak in 1972 and the Nautilus in 1976, the first steel sports watches with an integrated bracelet that cost as much as gold.

milestones.event: Drew the Royal Oak for Audemars Piguet, a steel watch with an octagonal bezel and eight screws.
Drew the Nautilus for Patek Philippe.

people.name: Dieter Rams
people.bio: German industrial designer of Braun products and the ten principles of good design.

milestones.event: Designed the SK 4 radio-phonograph with Hans Gugelot.
Designed the 606 universal shelving system on a grid of rails.
Became head of design at Braun.
Gave the talk that listed his principles of good design.

people.name: Eero Aarnio
people.bio: Finnish designer of the Ball chair and other fibreglass furniture in round forms.

milestones.event: Designed the Ball chair in fibreglass.

people.name: François Truffaut
people.bio: French critic and film director who attacked the old French cinema and then replaced it.

milestones.event: Published A Certain Tendency of the French Cinema.
Released The 400 Blows.

people.name: Michel Guérard
people.bio: French chef and pastry chef. He cooked at Asnières and at Eugénie-les-Bains, and made cuisine minceur for the guests of a spa. His restaurant Les Prés d'Eugénie held three Michelin stars from 1977.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Le Pot-au-Feu in Asnières-sur-Seine.
Moved to Eugénie-les-Bains and began his slimming cuisine for the spa guests.
Published La Grande Cuisine minceur; Time put him on its cover in February.
Les Prés d'Eugénie won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Richard Rogers
people.bio: British-Italian architect who put the services of a building on its outside.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris with Renzo Piano.
Completed the Lloyd's building in London.

people.name: Giorgio Armani
people.bio: Italian designer. His soft, unstructured jackets in plain wool set the line of the working suit for both sexes in the 1980s.

milestones.event: Founded his fashion house in Milan with Sergio Galeotti.
Dressed the lead of the film American Gigolo in soft, unstructured jackets.

people.name: Hilla Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Bernd Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Bernd Becher.

people.name: Michael Graves
people.bio: American architect of colourful Postmodern buildings and household objects.

milestones.event: Completed the Portland Building in Oregon.
Designed the 9093 kettle with a bird whistle for Alessi.

people.name: Paco Rabanne
people.bio: Spanish-born French designer. He built dresses from plastic discs and metal rings, and so made metal and plastic a material of couture.

milestones.event: Showed 12 Unwearable Dresses in Contemporary Materials, made of plastic discs and metal links.

people.name: Bodo Mans
people.bio: German ceramic designer who drew vases for the West German potteries of the 1960s and 1970s. His heavy forms carry the thick, running glazes of fat lava ware.

milestones.event: Designed vases for the Bay Keramik pottery in the mid 1960s, at the start of the fat lava years.

people.name: Geoffrey Lee
people.bio: British type designer who drew the Impact typeface. Meme makers later chose it for the captions of the image macro.

milestones.event: Drew Impact for the Stephenson Blake foundry.

people.name: Mario Buatta
people.bio: American decorator called the Prince of Chintz, whose layered English country rooms are the source of the grandmillennial look.

people.name: Norman Foster
people.bio: English architect of High-tech buildings that show their structure and services.

milestones.event: Completed the HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Victor Moscoso
people.bio: Spanish-American artist of psychedelic posters with vibrating colour.

milestones.event: Made posters for the Family Dog and the Matrix in San Francisco.

people.name: Renzo Piano
people.bio: Italian architect who designed the Centre Pompidou with Richard Rogers.

photo.credit: Cirone-Musi (Festival della Scienza, Genova)Color and edits by the uploader.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris.
Completed the Potsdamer Platz tower in Berlin, which has a terracotta facade.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Robert Adams
people.bio: American photographer of the suburban American West.

milestones.event: Published The New West.
Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Wes Wilson
people.bio: American artist who made the psychedelic concert poster with melting letters.

milestones.event: Made the first of his Fillmore posters for Bill Graham.

people.name: Issey Miyake
people.bio: Japanese designer. He pressed polyester jersey into permanent pleats after the garment was cut, and so made clothes that are light and stretch.

milestones.event: Launched the Pleats Please line of heat-set pleated polyester.

people.name: Joel Meyerowitz
people.bio: American photographer who moved street photography into colour.

milestones.event: Published Cape Light.

people.name: Marcello Gandini
people.bio: Italian car designer. At Bertone he drew the low, flat wedge with a sharp crease that set the line of the supercar for 20 years.

milestones.event: Drew the Carabo show car for Bertone.
Drew the Stratos Zero show car, a wedge that was 84 cm high.
Showed the Countach prototype.

people.name: Terry de Havilland
people.bio: English shoemaker from a London shoe family. He made the bright platforms and wedges that glam rock musicians wore in the 1970s.

milestones.event: Made new three-tiered wedge shoes in snakeskin colours, from a pair that he found in his father's attic.
Became the rock and roll cobbler of the decade; his clients included David Bowie and Led Zeppelin.

people.name: Yvon Chouinard
people.bio: American climber and maker. He made climbing gear in California, and in 1973 he began to sell outdoor clothes. His firm helped to make polar fleece.

milestones.event: Began to sell outdoor clothes under the name Patagonia.
Worked with Malden Mills on a napped polyester pile that became polar fleece.

people.name: Richard Serra
people.bio: American sculptor. Castelli found him in 1967 and offered three years of monthly payments.

milestones.event: Castelli offered him a guarantee of monthly payments.

people.name: William Eggleston
people.bio: American photographer who made colour photography accepted as art.

milestones.event: Showed William Eggleston's Guide at MoMA.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Nintendo who designed the Game Boy around a cheap four-shade monochrome screen.

milestones.event: Led the design of the Game Boy and its four-shade screen.

people.name: Vivienne Westwood
people.bio: British designer. With Malcolm McLaren she made the torn, pinned, slogan-printed and bondage clothes that dressed the London punk scene.

milestones.event: Opened a shop at 430 King's Road, London, with Malcolm McLaren.
Renamed the shop SEX and sold rubber, leather and bondage clothes.

people.name: Calvin Klein
people.bio: American designer who founded a fashion house in 1968. In the 1980s his name on the waistband made plain underwear a branded and advertised product.

milestones.event: Launched the company that later took his name.
Put his name on the waistband of a plain brief and sold it as fashion.

people.name: Jeremiah Tower
people.bio: American chef. He was the chef of Chez Panisse from 1972 to 1978 and gave the daily menu its sharp, ripe and formal style. In 1984 he opened Stars in San Francisco.

milestones.event: Joined Chez Panisse as a cook and later as its chef.
Opened the restaurant Stars in San Francisco.

people.name: Rei Kawakubo
people.bio: Japanese designer. She founded Comme des Garçons and made black, loose, torn and lopsided clothes that questioned the shape of the body.

milestones.event: Founded the Comme des Garçons label in Tokyo.
Showed her first collection in Paris, in black, loose and torn clothes.
Showed Body Meets Dress, Dress Meets Body, with padded lumps on the body.

people.name: Jil Sander
people.bio: German designer. Her plain, fine and precisely cut clothes in neutral colours set the line of 1990s minimalism.

milestones.event: Opened her first boutique in Hamburg.

people.name: Yohji Yamamoto
people.bio: Japanese designer. His long, black, oversized clothes in wool and cotton set the dark, loose line of the Japanese wave in Paris.

milestones.event: Showed his first collection in Paris, in loose black clothes.

people.name: Alice Waters
people.bio: American chef, author and food activist. She opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley in 1971 and built the menu on fresh, seasonal produce from named local farms. She also began the Edible Schoolyard project in a Berkeley school. She worked with a pottery on a dinnerware line for her restaurant.

milestones.event: Opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley.
Opened the Chez Panisse Café upstairs, with an à la carte menu.
Started the Chez Panisse Foundation and the Edible Schoolyard.
Worked with Heath Ceramics and Christina Kim on the Chez Panisse dinnerware collection.

people.name: Dapper Dan
people.bio: American tailor of Harlem, New York. In the 1980s he printed luxury logos on leather and made jackets, bags and car seats for his clients.

milestones.event: Opened his boutique on 125th Street, Harlem.
By the mid-1980s printed luxury logos on leather with a silk-screen press.

people.name: Massimo Osti
people.bio: Italian designer of Bologna. He took sport and military cloth into dress, dyed whole garments and tried new fabrics for C.P. Company and Stone Island.

milestones.event: Launched Stone Island with a jacket of heavy rubberised cloth of the type used for truck covers.

people.name: Lewis Baltz
people.bio: American photographer of industrial parks and new tract houses.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Patrick Le Quément
people.bio: French designer. He led the design of Renault from 1987 and made small cars with soft, round forms and bright interiors.

milestones.event: Became director of design at Renault.
Showed the Twingo, a one-box city car with a round body.

people.name: Ward Christensen
people.bio: American engineer who built the first bulletin board system, CBBS, with Randy Suess. It made the dial-up boards where ANSI art grew.

milestones.event: Started CBBS in Chicago with Randy Suess, the first public bulletin board system.

people.name: Malcolm McLaren
people.bio: British impresario and shop owner. He ran the King's Road shop with Vivienne Westwood and managed the Sex Pistols, who wore its clothes.

milestones.event: Ran the SEX shop at 430 King's Road, London.
Became the manager of the Sex Pistols, and dressed the band in the shop's clothes.

people.name: Mark Perry
people.bio: English writer and musician who started the punk fanzine Sniffin' Glue.

photo.credit: The original uploader was Wwwhatsup at English Wikipedia.

milestones.event: Started Sniffin' Glue while he worked as a bank clerk.
Stopped the zine and formed the band Alternative TV.

people.name: Michel Bras
people.bio: French chef of Laguiole in the Aubrac, who built his menu from the wild and garden plants of the plateau and made the plate a small landscape.

milestones.event: Took over the kitchen of the family restaurant in Laguiole and began to cook from the plants of the plateau.
Made the first gargouillou, a dish of dozens of young vegetables, herbs and flowers.
Moved the restaurant to a new building on the Suquet plateau above Laguiole.

people.name: Axel Vervoordt
people.bio: Belgian art dealer and interior designer of rooms in raw, quiet materials.

people.name: Jamie Reid
people.bio: British artist who made the ransom-note graphics of the Sex Pistols.

milestones.event: Made the cover of God Save the Queen.
Made the cover of Never Mind the Bollocks.

people.name: Stephen Shore
people.bio: American photographer of colour road trips across the United States.

photo.credit: Drpaluga (talk). Original uploader was Drpaluga at en.wikipedia

milestones.event: Published Uncommon Places.

people.name: Donna Karan
people.bio: American designer. Her 1985 Seven Easy Pieces gave the working woman a small wardrobe of bodysuit, skirt, jacket and trouser.

milestones.event: Showed Seven Easy Pieces, a system of work clothes for women.

people.name: Ed Logg
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made arcade games for vector and raster screens.

milestones.event: Co-designed Asteroids, a vector-display arcade game.

people.name: Scott Fahlman
people.bio: American computer scientist who proposed :-) and :-( on a Carnegie Mellon message board in 1982.

milestones.event: Proposed :-) and :-( as marks for jokes and serious posts on a Carnegie Mellon message board.

people.name: Steve Wilhite
people.bio: American computer scientist who led the CompuServe team that made the GIF image format.

milestones.event: Led the team at CompuServe that released the GIF format.

people.name: John Pawson
people.bio: British architect who reduces a room to light, proportion and one material, with all storage hidden.

milestones.event: Completed the Calvin Klein flagship store on Madison Avenue, New York.
Published the book Minimum.

people.name: Nobu Matsuhisa
people.bio: Japanese chef who worked in Peru and Argentina before Los Angeles. He cooked Japanese fish with Peruvian chilli and citrus and opened Matsuhisa in 1987 and Nobu in New York in 1994.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Matsuhisa in Los Angeles.
Opened the first Nobu in New York with Robert De Niro and partners.

people.name: Philippe Starck
people.bio: French designer. His first sanitary ware range for Duravit in 1994 treated a washbasin and a WC as designed objects, not as plain fittings.

milestones.event: Launched his first sanitary ware collection for Duravit.

people.name: Tom Truscott
people.bio: American computer scientist. As a graduate student at Duke University he planned Usenet with Jim Ellis, a news network between Unix computers.

milestones.event: Planned Usenet with Jim Ellis at Duke University.

people.name: Wolfgang Puck
people.bio: Austrian-American chef trained in France. He opened Spago in Los Angeles in 1982 and Chinois on Main in Santa Monica in 1983, where he put Chinese flavours on a French and Californian plate.

milestones.event: Opened Spago on the Sunset Strip in Los Angeles.
Opened Chinois on Main in Santa Monica.

people.name: Ken Kutaragi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Sony who led the design of the PlayStation and its polygon hardware.

milestones.event: Led the launch of the PlayStation in Japan.

people.name: Zaha Hadid
people.bio: Iraqi-British architect of fractured and then fluid forms, the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize.

milestones.event: Showed her work in the Deconstructivist Architecture show at MoMA.
Completed the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Dave Theurer
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made colour vector arcade games with deep perspective.

milestones.event: Designed Tempest, a colour vector game seen down a tube in perspective.

people.name: Michele De Lucchi
people.bio: Italian architect and designer, a founding member of the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Joined the Memphis Group as a founding member.
Designed the Tolomeo lamp with Giancarlo Fassina.

people.name: Jean Paul Gaultier
people.bio: French designer who used the corset as a motif of his work and took the boned bodice and the cone bra out of the underwear drawer and on to the runway.

milestones.event: Introduced the corset with a cone bra for women.
Made the cone-bra costumes for the Blond Ambition tour of Madonna.

people.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
people.bio: Japanese game designer at Nintendo who set the look of side-scrolling and top-down worlds on 8-bit hardware.

milestones.event: Directed Super Mario Bros. on an 8×8 tile grid.
Directed Super Mario 64, a free 3D camera world.

people.name: Brunello Cucinelli
people.bio: Italian designer and maker. He built a house on cashmere in soft colours and fine hand finish, made in Solomeo, Umbria, with no visible logo.

milestones.event: Began his firm with a small line of cashmere jumpers in colour.
Founded his firm with a small range of coloured cashmere jumpers.

people.name: Elmar Mock
people.bio: Swiss engineer. With Jacques Müller he built the first plastic watch of few parts, which became the Swatch.

milestones.event: Launched the Swatch watch with Jacques Müller and Ernst Thomke.

people.name: Nan Goldin
people.bio: American photographer of her own circle at night, lit by direct flash.

milestones.event: Published The Ballad of Sexual Dependency.

people.name: J Mays
people.bio: American car designer. He drew the Concept One show car for Volkswagen, and from 1997 he led design at Ford, where he revived old forms.

milestones.event: Showed the Concept One at the Detroit show.
Became vice president of design at Ford.

people.name: Shawn Stussy
people.bio: American surfboard shaper. He printed his hand-written name on T-shirts and shorts, and so began one of the first streetwear labels.

milestones.event: Began to sell T-shirts and shorts with his signature mark, from Laguna Beach, California.

people.name: Tim O'Reilly
people.bio: Irish-American publisher who helped name Web 2.0 at a conference in 2004 and set out its ideas in an essay in 2005.

milestones.event: Held the first Web 2.0 Conference with John Battelle; the term spread to site design.

people.name: David Carson
people.bio: American graphic designer of layered, broken magazine type.

milestones.event: Became art director of Ray Gun magazine.
Published The End of Print.

people.name: Hervé This
people.bio: French physical chemist who studies the changes of food in the kitchen and who named the science of molecular and physical gastronomy with Nicholas Kurti.

milestones.event: Founded the workshop on molecular and physical gastronomy with Nicholas Kurti in Erice, Sicily.
Published Molecular Gastronomy: Exploring the Science of Flavor in English.

people.name: Lisa Frank
people.bio: American designer who founded a stationery company known for rainbow colours, bright animals and sticker sheets. Kidcore takes much from her 1980s and 1990s look.

milestones.event: Founded Lisa Frank Inc. in Tucson, Arizona.

people.name: David Bohnett
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Beverly Hills Internet, which became GeoCities, the free host of personal home pages.

milestones.event: The company Beverly Hills Internet took the name GeoCities.

people.name: Helmut Lang
people.bio: Austrian designer. His slim, plain and exact clothes in black, white and grey set a clean, urban line in the 1990s.

milestones.event: Founded his own label in Vienna.

people.name: Ian Anderson
people.bio: British graphic designer who founded The Designers Republic.

milestones.event: Founded The Designers Republic in Sheffield.
Designed the graphics of the game Wipeout.

people.name: Jim Ellis
people.bio: American computer scientist. With Tom Truscott at Duke University he planned Usenet, a network of discussion groups that started in 1980.

milestones.event: Planned Usenet with Tom Truscott at Duke University.

people.name: Lars von Trier
people.bio: Danish film director who wrote the Dogme 95 manifesto with Thomas Vinterberg.

milestones.event: Signed the Dogme 95 manifesto in Copenhagen.
Released The Idiots, Dogme #2.

people.name: Naoto Fukasawa
people.bio: Japanese industrial designer of quiet household products, and co-author of the Super Normal idea.

milestones.event: Showed the Super Normal exhibition in Tokyo with Jasper Morrison.

people.name: Roy Yamaguchi
people.bio: Japanese-American chef who trained in French kitchens. In 1988 he opened Roy's in Honolulu, and in 1991 he was one of the chefs who named Hawaii regional cuisine.

milestones.event: Opened the first Roy's restaurant in Honolulu.
Joined the chefs who gave Hawaii regional cuisine its name.

people.name: Yasushi Wakabayashi
people.bio: Japanese net user whom sources credit with an early upright emoticon, (^_^), posted on the ASCII NET bulletin board in 1986.

milestones.event: Posted the face (^_^) on the ASCII NET board, an early example of the Japanese upright kaomoji style.

people.name: Nathalie Du Pasquier
people.bio: French artist who drew the patterns of the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Joined the Memphis Group as a founding member.

people.name: Neville Brody
people.bio: British graphic designer and art director of The Face magazine.

milestones.event: Became art director of The Face.
Published The Graphic Language of Neville Brody.

people.name: Chris Stamper
people.bio: British programmer who co-founded Ultimate Play the Game and wrote its isometric engine.

milestones.event: Co-made Knight Lore, whose room engine set the isometric look on home computers.

people.name: Jasper Morrison
people.bio: British designer of plain, useful furniture and household objects, who named the Super Normal idea with Naoto Fukasawa.

milestones.event: Designed the Plywood chair for a Swiss furniture firm.
Showed the Super Normal exhibition in Tokyo with Naoto Fukasawa.

people.name: Nathan Myhrvold
people.bio: American physicist and former technology chief of Microsoft, who led the team of The Cooking Lab that wrote the six-volume book Modernist Cuisine.

milestones.event: Published Modernist Cuisine: The Art and Science of Cooking with Chris Young and Maxime Bilet.

people.name: Rand Miller
people.bio: American game designer who co-founded Cyan and co-made Myst from pre-rendered stills.

milestones.event: Co-made Myst with his brother Robyn.

people.name: Emma Bridgewater
people.bio: British potter and businesswoman. In 1985 she started a pottery in Stoke-on-Trent that makes sponge-decorated earthenware, and brought spongeware back into common use.

milestones.event: Started her pottery with sponge-decorated mugs and jugs.

people.name: Silvia Venturini Fendi
people.bio: Italian designer of accessories, a third-generation member of the Fendi family. She designed the Baguette in 1997, a small beaded bag worn under the arm.

milestones.event: Designed the Baguette, a short-strap bag that the house sold in hundreds of surfaces.

people.name: Hillman Curtis
people.bio: American designer and film maker who showed how Flash could make motion graphics for the web, and who wrote a book about it.

milestones.event: Published Flash Web Design, a guide to design in Flash.

people.name: Tim Stamper
people.bio: British game developer who co-founded Ultimate Play the Game and later Rare.

milestones.event: Co-made Knight Lore with its isometric room engine.

people.name: Ferran Adrià
people.bio: Catalan chef of elBulli on the Costa Brava, who made the foam, the sphere and the deconstructed dish into the language of a new kitchen.

milestones.event: Became head chef of elBulli in Roses.
Served the first siphon foams at elBulli.
Made spherification a dish at elBulli, with sodium alginate and a calcium bath.
Closed the restaurant elBulli and turned it into a foundation.

people.name: India Mahdavi
people.bio: Iranian-born French architect and designer of rooms in saturated colour.

milestones.event: Redesigned The Gallery at Sketch in London in pink.

people.name: Claus Meyer
people.bio: Danish food entrepreneur who co-founded Noma and wrote the Manifesto for the New Nordic Kitchen in 2004.

milestones.event: Co-founded Noma with René Redzepi.
Called the Nordic Cuisine Symposium, where twelve chefs signed the manifesto.

people.name: Donna Tartt
people.bio: American novelist. Her novel The Secret History tells of a small circle of classics students, and it is the main text behind dark academia.

milestones.event: Published The Secret History.

people.name: Eiji Aonuma
people.bio: Japanese game director at Nintendo who directed a cel-shaded 3D world.

milestones.event: Directed The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.bio: American basketball player. His signed shoe of 1985 made the sneaker a badge of taste and a collector item.

milestones.event: His first signature shoe, the Air Jordan 1, went on sale in black and red.

people.name: Juergen Teller
people.bio: German photographer of raw, flash-lit fashion pictures.

people.name: Naoto Ohshima
people.bio: Japanese artist at Sega who designed characters and worlds for fast 16-bit parallax games.

milestones.event: Designed the hero and art of Sonic the Hedgehog.

people.name: Stefan Sonnenfeld
people.bio: American colourist who graded blockbusters in teal and orange.

milestones.event: Graded Transformers.

people.name: Yves Camdeborde
people.bio: French chef trained at the Ritz, La Tour d'Argent and the Hôtel de Crillon. In 1992 he bought La Régalade in Paris, cooked there at a low fixed price, and gave the bistro style a name that the press called bistronomie.

milestones.event: Bought the restaurant La Régalade in the 14th arrondissement of Paris.
Opened Le Comptoir du Relais in the Saint-Germain quarter.

people.name: Kazuko Shibuya
people.bio: Japanese pixel artist at Square who drew sprites and maps for 8-bit and 16-bit role-playing games.

milestones.event: Drew the pixel sprites of Final Fantasy.
Drew pixel art for Final Fantasy VI.

people.name: Michael Bay
people.bio: American film director whose action films made the teal and orange grade common.

milestones.event: Released Transformers.

people.name: Shinji Mikami
people.bio: Japanese game director at Capcom who used pre-rendered rooms and fixed cameras for suspense.

milestones.event: Directed Resident Evil with pre-rendered rooms.

people.name: Frédérick Raynal
people.bio: French game designer who put polygon figures over fixed, drawn camera views.

milestones.event: Made Alone in the Dark with fixed camera angles over drawn rooms.

people.name: Heston Blumenthal
people.bio: English chef of The Fat Duck in Bray, who used the lessons of food science, low-temperature cooking and play with memory to build long tasting menus.

milestones.event: Opened The Fat Duck in Bray, Berkshire.
Published The Big Fat Duck Cookbook.

people.name: Robyn Miller
people.bio: American artist and composer who rendered the worlds of Myst in 3D software.

milestones.event: Rendered the island views of Myst.

people.name: Gastón Acurio
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Lima, who took ceviche and the native produce of Peru into fine dining and led the rise of Peruvian cuisine in the world.

milestones.event: Opened Astrid y Gastón in Lima with Astrid Gutsche.
Founded Mistura, the yearly food fair of Lima, to show Peruvian produce and cooks.

people.name: Jony Ive
people.bio: British designer who led design at Apple, from the translucent iMac to the flat interface of iOS 7.

milestones.event: Released the iMac G3 in translucent Bondi Blue.
Released the first iPhone.
Released iOS 7, a flat interface, as head of Human Interface design.
Led the design team that released the Apple Watch.
Left Apple and founded LoveFrom.

people.name: Franz von Holzhausen
people.bio: American car designer. He led the design of the Model S, a saloon with a smooth body and one large screen in place of a dashboard.

milestones.event: Joined Tesla as chief designer.
The Model S went on sale.

people.name: Jerry Yang
people.bio: Co-founder of Yahoo!. He and David Filo began a link directory in 1994 that grew into the model of the web portal.

milestones.event: Started the Yahoo! link directory with David Filo.

people.name: Justin Sewell
people.bio: A founder of Despair, Inc., the company that sold the Demotivators line of black-framed posters from 1998.

milestones.event: Despair, Inc. began to sell Demotivators, posters that invert the office motivational poster.

people.name: Scott Forstall
people.bio: American software engineer who led iOS at Apple in its skeuomorphic years.

milestones.event: Released the first iPhone OS as head of the software team.
Left Apple after the iOS 6 Maps launch.

people.name: Thomas Vinterberg
people.bio: Danish film director who co-wrote the Dogme 95 manifesto.

milestones.event: Signed the Dogme 95 manifesto.
Released Festen, Dogme #1.

people.name: James Atkinson
people.bio: Software developer who started phpBB, a free and open-source forum program, in 2000.

milestones.event: Started phpBB, a free forum program.

people.name: Tim Sweeney
people.bio: American programmer who founded Epic Games and leads Unreal Engine.

milestones.event: Made Unreal Engine 4, with physically based materials, open to all for a subscription.

people.name: Tom Anderson
people.bio: American co-founder of Myspace. His profile was the first friend of each new member.

milestones.event: Co-founded Myspace.

people.name: Andoni Luis Aduriz
people.bio: Basque chef of Mugaritz near San Sebastián, who joined wild plants, odd texture and a play on the senses in one tasting menu.

milestones.event: Opened Mugaritz in Errenteria, in the hills near San Sebastián.
Published Mugaritz: A Natural Science of Cooking with Phaidon.

people.name: Olia Lialina
people.bio: Russian net artist. Her work My Boyfriend Came Back from the War used frames and plain HTML to tell a story in the browser window.

milestones.event: Published My Boyfriend Came Back from the War, a story told in nested browser frames.

people.name: Samwise Didier
people.bio: American art director at Blizzard who set its chunky, hand-painted fantasy look.

milestones.event: Art director of World of Warcraft.

people.name: Sara Blakely
people.bio: American businesswoman. She founded Spanx in Atlanta, and her footless control-top tights started the modern line of shapewear.

milestones.event: Founded Spanx in Atlanta and sold footless control-top tights.

people.name: Yusuke Naora
people.bio: Japanese art director at Square who led the pre-rendered city and room art of Final Fantasy VII.

milestones.event: Art director of Final Fantasy VII.

people.name: Shigetaka Kurita
people.bio: Japanese designer who drew the first widely used emoji set, of 176 pictures on a 12 by 12 pixel grid, for the NTT Docomo i-mode phone.

milestones.event: NTT Docomo released his set of 176 emoji, drawn in 1998 on a 12 by 12 pixel grid, on its i-mode service.

people.name: Harmony Korine
people.bio: American filmmaker who shot on VHS and made a Dogme 95 film.

milestones.event: Released Julien Donkey-Boy, a Dogme 95 film.
Released Trash Humpers, shot on VHS.

people.name: Matías Duarte
people.bio: Chilean designer who led the creation of Material Design at Google.

milestones.event: Presented Material Design at Google I/O.

people.name: Phoebe Philo
people.bio: British designer. As creative director of Céline from 2008 she made plain, calm clothes in fine cloth that others took as the model of quiet luxury.

milestones.event: Became creative director of Céline and made plain, fine clothes with no visible logo.

people.name: Grant Achatz
people.bio: American chef of Alinea in Chicago, who turned the methods of the modernist kitchen into a tasting menu with edible balloons, hot and cold soups and a play of scent.

milestones.event: Opened Alinea in Chicago.
Published the book Alinea with Nick Kokonas.

people.name: Kikiyama
people.bio: Japanese game maker who made the free game Yume Nikki in 2004. Its dream rooms and strange places became a source of the dream image look.

milestones.event: Released Yume Nikki, a game about a girl who explores dream worlds.

people.name: Cliff Bleszinski
people.bio: American game designer at Epic who led a gritty, desaturated HD shooter.

milestones.event: Lead designer of Gears of War.

people.name: Daniel Humm
people.bio: Swiss-born chef of Eleven Madison Park in New York, who changed the menu of a three-star restaurant to plant-based food in 2021, and put some animal products back in 2025.

milestones.event: Reopened Eleven Madison Park with a menu of plant-based food only.
Published Eleven Madison Park: The Plant-Based Cookbook.

people.name: Jack Dorsey
people.bio: American co-founder of Twitter, the site whose post card gave the tweet screenshot meme its frame.

milestones.event: Co-founded Twitter and sent the first public post.

people.name: René Redzepi
people.bio: Danish chef of Noma in Copenhagen, who made foraging, fermentation and the Nordic season the frame of a tasting menu.

milestones.event: Opened Noma in Copenhagen with Claus Meyer.
Noma was first named the best restaurant of the World's 50 Best list.
Published The Noma Guide to Fermentation with David Zilber.

people.name: Virgilio Martínez
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Central in Lima, who organises the menu by altitude and uses tubers, grains and plants from the sea to the high Andes.

milestones.event: Opened Central in Lima.

people.name: Tomoya Asano
people.bio: Japanese producer at Square Enix who started the HD-2D look.

milestones.event: Produced Octopath Traveler, the first HD-2D game.

people.name: Markus Persson
people.bio: Swedish programmer who made Minecraft and founded Mojang.

milestones.event: Released the first version of Minecraft.

people.name: Mitsuharu Tsumura
people.bio: Peruvian chef of Japanese family, known as Micha, who leads Maido in Lima and set the form of Nikkei cuisine at the top of the table.

milestones.event: Opened Maido, a Nikkei restaurant, in Lima.

people.name: Zach Barth
people.bio: American game developer who made Infiniminer, an early block-mining game.

milestones.event: Released Infiniminer, a world of mineable cubes.

people.name: Albert Shum
people.bio: Designer who led the Metro design language of Windows Phone, with its grid of live tiles.

milestones.event: Released the tile grid of Windows Phone 7 as its design lead.

people.name: Jennifer Allen
people.bio: The forum user who proposed the name autonomous sensory meridian response (ASMR) in 2010.

milestones.event: Proposed the name autonomous sensory meridian response for the effect.

people.name: Lewis Hilsenteger
people.bio: Canadian-American video maker who runs the Unbox Therapy channel, a model of the plain, top-down unboxing video.

milestones.event: Started the Unbox Therapy channel on YouTube.

people.name: Casey Neistat
people.bio: American filmmaker and YouTuber who made the daily vlog a cinematic form.

milestones.event: Started his daily vlog on YouTube.
Founded Beme, a video app.

people.name: Greg Lutze
people.bio: Co-creator of VSCO, the photo app that made preset codes such as A6 a common way to edit.

milestones.event: Co-created VSCO Cam with Joel Flory.

people.name: Jamie Beck
people.bio: American photographer who made the first cinemagraphs with the motion designer Kevin Burg in 2011.

milestones.event: Released the first cinemagraphs with Kevin Burg during New York Fashion Week.

people.name: Joel Flory
people.bio: Co-creator of VSCO, the photo app whose film-stock presets set a matte look for phone photos.

milestones.event: Co-created VSCO Cam with Greg Lutze, a photo app with film-style presets.

people.name: Kevin Burg
people.bio: American motion designer who made cinemagraphs with the photographer Jamie Beck from 2011.

milestones.event: Built the looping motion of the first cinemagraphs with Jamie Beck.

people.name: Lil Internet
people.bio: American DJ who used the word seapunk in a joke tweet in 2011. The word named the ocean theme that spread online.

milestones.event: Posted the word seapunk in a tweet about a leather jacket with barnacles.

people.name: Nathan Williams
people.bio: Co-founder of Kinfolk magazine, whose calm, natural-light still lifes of tables and objects shaped the flat lay look.

milestones.event: Co-founded Kinfolk, a magazine of slow-living photo spreads.

people.name: Sahil Lavingia
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Gumroad, whose 2021 redesign made Neo-Brutalism popular.

milestones.event: Founded Gumroad.
Released the Neo-Brutalist redesign of Gumroad.

people.name: Takeshi Idezawa
people.bio: Japanese executive of the company behind the LINE messenger, which launched in 2011 and made sticker packs a core part of chat.

milestones.event: Led the company that launched the LINE messenger, later known for its sticker packs.

people.name: Daniel Lopatin
people.bio: American musician whose slowed loops prepared the sound of Vaporwave.

milestones.event: Released Chuck Person's Eccojams Vol. 1.

people.name: Eric Migicovsky
people.bio: Canadian engineer who founded Pebble. His crowd-funded smartwatch of 2012 raised more money than any project before it on Kickstarter.

milestones.event: Raised funds for the Pebble smartwatch on Kickstarter.

people.name: A. G. Cook
people.bio: British producer and founder of the label PC Music. Spotify editors call him a godfather of hyperpop.

milestones.event: Founded PC Music, whose cover art mixes pastel gloss, 3D and web clutter.

people.name: Alan Dye
people.bio: American designer who led the Human Interface team at Apple.

milestones.event: Worked on the user interface of iOS 7.
Presented the interface of visionOS.

people.name: Alexis Ohanian
people.bio: American co-founder of Reddit, a main home of deep-fried and surreal meme communities.

milestones.event: Co-founded Reddit.

people.name: Emily Segal
people.bio: American writer and trend forecaster. She co-founded the trend group K-Hole, whose 2013 report Youth Mode brought the word normcore into use.

milestones.event: Took part in the K-Hole report Youth Mode, which named normcore as a choice to blend in.

people.name: Greta Gerwig
people.bio: American director and writer. Her film Barbie and its pink sets and costumes set off the Barbiecore trend in fashion and online images.

milestones.event: Released the film Barbie, which carried the pink look to a mass audience.

people.name: Justin Kan
people.bio: American founder of Justin.tv, the live video site from which the game stream platform Twitch grew.

milestones.event: Launched Twitch as a game-only branch of Justin.tv.

people.name: Kevin Systrom
people.bio: Co-founder of Instagram, the app that added the swipe carousel post in 2017.

milestones.event: Co-launched Instagram, with filters and square photos.
Led Instagram as the feed moved to a ranked order and profiles became curated grids.
Led Instagram as it added posts with up to 10 photos in one swipeable carousel.

people.name: Mike Grabarek
people.bio: Co-founder of the first Health Goth group on Facebook. The group mixed goth mood, sport and net art images.

milestones.event: Started the Health Goth Facebook community with Jeremy Scott and Chris Cantino.

people.name: Rosa Menkman
people.bio: Dutch artist and theorist of glitch art, author of the Glitch Studies Manifesto and The Glitch Moment(um).

milestones.event: Published the Glitch Studies Manifesto, a text on the creative use of errors.
Published The Glitch Moment(um) with the Institute of Network Cultures.

people.name: Steve Huffman
people.bio: American programmer who co-founded Reddit with Alexis Ohanian and wrote much of its first code.

milestones.event: Co-founded Reddit.

people.name: Zhang Yiming
people.bio: Founder of ByteDance, the company behind Douyin, TikTok and CapCut.

milestones.event: ByteDance merged Musical.ly into TikTok, the app that carries the Duet tool.
ByteDance launched CapCut, the editor with the velocity tool.

people.name: Alex Zhu
people.bio: Co-founder of Musical.ly, the short-video app where users mimed songs in 15-second clips.

milestones.event: Co-founded Musical.ly, an app for 15-second lip-sync videos.

people.name: Ken Wong
people.bio: Australian game artist who was lead designer of Monument Valley at ustwo.

milestones.event: Lead designer of Monument Valley.

people.name: Tony Zhou
people.bio: Video maker who made the series Every Frame a Painting with Taylor Ramos, short film essays with clean type and clips.

milestones.event: Started the series Every Frame a Painting on Vimeo and YouTube.

people.name: Alexander Mordvintsev
people.bio: Researcher at Google who wrote the code that made DeepDream, the first widely shared neural network image effect.

milestones.event: Wrote the DeepDream code and posted its first images at Google.

people.name: Antonio Guillem
people.bio: Spanish photographer whose stock photo of three people on a street became the base of the Distracted Boyfriend label meme.

milestones.event: Took the stock photo that the label meme later used.

people.name: Jason Citron
people.bio: American entrepreneur who co-founded Discord, a chat app for communities that began with gamers.

milestones.event: Launched Discord with Stanislav Vishnevskiy.

people.name: The Cobrasnake
people.bio: American nightlife photographer whose direct-flash party photos defined the 2000s blog era.

people.name: Tobias van Schneider
people.bio: German designer who led product design at Spotify and set trends in flat interface and brand design.

milestones.event: Worked on the duotone brand of Spotify as lead designer.

people.name: David Karp
people.bio: American entrepreneur who founded Tumblr, the blog site where reblogged photo feeds spread the soft grunge look.

milestones.event: Founded Tumblr, a microblog site built on reblogged images.

people.name: Justus Thies
people.bio: German computer scientist who co-wrote Face2Face, a real-time method that carries one face's expression onto another face in video.

milestones.event: Co-wrote Face2Face, a real-time face re-enactment method for video.

people.name: Morikura En
people.bio: A Japanese illustrator. The Kizuna AI article credits Morikura with the character design of Kizuna AI, the first channel that called itself a virtual YouTuber.

milestones.event: Drew the character design of Kizuna AI, the anime-style avatar of the first virtual YouTuber.

people.name: Vincent Van Duysen
people.bio: Belgian architect and designer of calm interiors in natural materials.

milestones.event: Became creative director of Molteni&C.

people.name: Michelle Phan
people.bio: American video maker whose make-up tutorials on YouTube set a model for talk-while-you-prepare videos.

milestones.event: Posted make-up tutorial videos on YouTube.

people.name: Xoana Herrera
people.bio: Illustrator who drew Alegria, the illustration system that started Corporate Memphis.

milestones.event: Drew the Alegria illustration system for Facebook at Buck.

people.name: Breogán Hackett
people.bio: Irish game developer who founded Haunted PS1, a community for games in the style of the first PlayStation.

milestones.event: Founded Haunted PS1.
Released the Haunted PS1 Demo Disc.

people.name: Christopher Poole
people.bio: American founder of 4chan, the imageboard where the rage comic, the image macro and the wojak face spread.

milestones.event: Founded the imageboard 4chan.
Opened 4chan on the model of the Japanese board Futaba Channel.

people.name: Tero Karras
people.bio: Researcher at NVIDIA and lead author of StyleGAN, the face generator behind the generated headshot.

milestones.event: Published StyleGAN with Samuli Laine and Timo Aila.

people.name: Alexander Plyuto
people.bio: Ukrainian designer whose Skeuomorph Mobile Banking shot started the Neumorphism trend.

milestones.event: Posted the Skeuomorph Mobile Banking shot on Dribbble.

people.name: Felix Kjellberg
people.bio: Swedish video maker whose gameplay videos with a face window and loud captions set the form of the facecam commentary.

milestones.event: Opened the YouTube channel that later became the model of gameplay with a facecam.

people.name: Michal Malewicz
people.bio: Polish designer who named Glassmorphism and Neumorphism in his articles.

milestones.event: Named the trend Neumorphism in an article.
Named the trend Glassmorphism in an article.

people.name: Olivier van Herpt
people.bio: Dutch designer who builds his own clay printers and prints vessels in earthenware and stoneware. The wall of each vase shows the layer lines of the printer.

milestones.event: Showed vases from a clay printer that he built himself.

people.name: Taylor Swift
people.bio: American singer and songwriter. Her 2020 album Folklore, with its forest and cabin images, took cottagecore to a wide audience.

emblem.credit: Original: Taylor Swift / UMG Vector: SINGmeAsadSONG

milestones.event: Released the album Folklore, which pop media linked with the cottagecore look.

people.name: Alexis Barreyat
people.bio: French developer who co-created BeReal, the app that posts a back and a front camera photo at the same time.

milestones.event: Released BeReal with Kévin Perreau.

people.name: Zach King
people.bio: American filmmaker of short magic edits on Vine and TikTok.

milestones.event: Became known for six-second magic edits on Vine.

people.name: Jane Remover
people.bio: American musician. Wikipedia calls her the face of digicore, the music scene that grew with glitchcore edits.

milestones.event: Spread digicore sound and a fast, glitch look in the scene on SoundCloud and Discord.

people.name: Jay Christensen
people.bio: American drone pilot whose one-shot FPV flight through a bowling alley made cinematic FPV widely known.

milestones.event: Flew the one-shot FPV film Right Up Our Alley in Minneapolis.

people.name: Boris Dayma
people.bio: Machine learning engineer who made DALL-E Mini, the free image model that later took the name Craiyon.

milestones.event: His DALL-E Mini model went viral and filled feeds with 3x3 smudge grids.

people.name: Kane Parsons
people.bio: American filmmaker and creator who posts as Kane Pixels. His Backrooms videos gave the empty-room look of liminal spaces a story and a wide audience.

milestones.event: Posted The Backrooms (Found Footage) on YouTube.

people.name: Kyle Edward Ball
people.bio: Canadian film maker. He directed Skinamarink in 2022 and said that he looked at the online Weirdcore and Liminalspace groups while he worked on it.

milestones.event: Directed Skinamarink, a film with a low-quality, empty-house look that readers link to weirdcore.

people.name: Maxime Heckel
people.bio: Design engineer who writes about WebGL, shaders and 3D effects in the browser.

milestones.event: Published The Study of Shaders with React Three Fiber.
Spoke at Figma Config 2025.

people.name: Robin Rombach
people.bio: Researcher and lead author of the latent diffusion paper, the base of Stable Diffusion and of the glossy image look of open text-to-image models.

milestones.event: Latent diffusion paper appeared at CVPR; its method became the base of Stable Diffusion.

people.name: Vektroid
people.bio: American musician who made Floral Shoppe, the album that set the look of Vaporwave.

milestones.event: Released Floral Shoppe as Macintosh Plus.

people.name: Emil Kowalski
people.bio: Design engineer who worked at Vercel and Linear and makes open-source interface components with detailed motion.

milestones.event: Released Sonner, a toast component for React.

people.name: Simon Willison
people.bio: British programmer and writer who promoted the word slop for unwanted AI-made content in 2024.

milestones.event: Wrote a widely shared post that made slop the common name for unwanted AI-made content.

people.name: Hailey Bieber
people.bio: American model and founder of a skin-care brand. Media link her dewy skin, slick bun and neutral dress with the clean girl look.

milestones.event: Launched the skin-care brand Rhode, with a glazed skin look as its image.

people.name: MrBeast
people.bio: American video maker whose thumbnails, with a large face, a few words and strong colour, are a model of the clickbait still.

milestones.event: Gained a large audience with stunt videos that used bold, face-led thumbnails.

people.name: Khaby Lame
people.bio: Senegalese-Italian creator of silent short videos, for a time the most-followed person on TikTok.

milestones.event: Became the most-followed person on TikTok.
